Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

stab verb

also stab to death, prick, stabbing

classical

Sall. C. 60.7: ibique pugnāns cōnfoditur
Liv. 24.7.5 (Lewis & Short)

cōnfodiō, cōnfodere, cōnfōdī, cōnfossum

verb, third conjugation

stab, run through

Literally to dig all over (Cato, of the soil); in Sallust, Livy and Suetonius the word for stabbing someone, usually to death. Long ō before nf.

Other words

  • compungō, compungere, compūnxī, compūnctum — prick, sting

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.6.3: collum dolōne (Lewis & Short)

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short). For pricking with a pin or a needle, or a sting.

Examples

  • vidē nē dolōne collum compungam tibi

    mind I don’t prick your neck with my stingPhaedr. 3.6.3

  • Cavē nē tē acū compungās.

    Mind you don’t prick yourself with the needle.composed

See also kill, knife, dig, wound.

SourcesLewis & Short: confodio · Lewis & Short: compungo
